focus: E5: the third check plane (per-hub doctor + skill-local umbrella), severity semantics, costs, and the scoped commit-time fix
noveltyJustification: All 9 findings are new to this research; the severity mechanics and the umbrella's lack of callers are first recorded here.
answeredQuestions: Q5: E5 - What is the root cause of doctor (5e, 5i, 13c, 13d) and router-sync checks catching drift only after the fact, and the smallest fix that moves detection to the author's edit?

label: 5e and 5i are hard-by-default structural router checks (tieBreak permutation; workflow modes sort first) reported through softFail.
13c is advise-only on the four hubs listed in README_VERSION_WARN_ONLY; the checker exits 0 with that drift live.
parent-skill-check runs only in the doctor route and CI; neither is the author's edit surface.
One hub's checker costs ~1.96s measured — cheap for a scoped commit-time call, too slow fleet-wide per commit.
The router-sync umbrella exists with full leg coverage and one exit code and has no workflow or hook caller; only skill docs reference it.
The commit-time plane already gates sibling families (route-remint, mirror parity), so the E5 rules' fix is an extension of an existing dispatcher.
An unwired leg's cost is recorded: nine orphan docs and a tenth passed every gate while leg 1b was held back.
E5 root cause: the rule families live on a third check plane with no trigger from the edit loop; the two per-commit planes cover other families.
Smallest fix: empty the warn lists after repair, then extend the pre-commit staged-hub dispatch to call the scoped per-hub checker and the sk-code umbrella; first step before CI-only wiring.
